research_goal: Understand how the participant experiences AI in their workplace, including how it fits into their day-to-day work, how they make use of it, and what it changes for them.

plan.goal: Understand how AI shows up in the participant’s regular work and what they use it for today.
Learn how the participant first began using AI at work and what prompted that change.
Explore how AI affects the participant’s workflow, effort, or confidence in getting work done.
Understand what the participant worries about or would want to change about AI in their workplace experience.

turns.lead_in: Thanks for joining—I'd like to hear about AI in your workplace.
turns.question: How does AI show up in your regular work these days?
turns.answer: I use ChatGPT every morning to draft emails and summarise long threads. It probably saves me an hour a day.

turns.lead_in: You use ChatGPT as part of your morning routine.
turns.question: What was happening at work when you first decided to start using it?
turns.answer: A colleague showed me how it summarised a 40-page RFP in seconds. I was sceptical, but I tried it on my own backlog that same week.

turns.lead_in: That first demo and the backlog test sound like a real turning point.
turns.question: How has using ChatGPT changed the way you get through your morning work?
turns.answer: Our team ships reports twice as fast now. Honestly the hallucinations drive me crazy though, so I always double check numbers before anything goes to a client.

turns.lead_in: You’re moving faster, while still checking the numbers carefully.
turns.question: What’s the main change you’d want in ChatGPT for your client work?
turns.answer: I hope it gets more reliable, but I worry about junior roles. Writing first drafts is how I learned the job.

summary.overview: The participant uses ChatGPT as a regular morning tool to speed up email drafting and summarising, and says it saves substantial time. They were initially sceptical but became willing to try it after seeing a colleague use it, and now view it as useful but unreliable, especially for client-facing work. Their overall stance is mixed: they value the efficiency gains while worrying about hallucinations and what AI may mean for junior roles.

findings.finding: The participant uses ChatGPT every morning for drafting emails and summarising long threads, and sees it as a meaningful time-saver.
findings.quote: I use ChatGPT every morning to draft emails and summarise long threads.

findings.finding: The participant started using AI after a colleague demonstrated a fast RFP summary, and initial scepticism gave way to trying it on their own work the same week.
findings.quote: A colleague showed me how it summarised a 40-page RFP in seconds. I was sceptical, but I tried it

findings.finding: ChatGPT has sped up the team's report production, but the participant still double-checks outputs because errors make them wary.
findings.quote: Our team ships reports twice as fast now.

findings.finding: The participant wants ChatGPT to be more reliable and is concerned it could reduce opportunities for junior staff to learn through first-draft writing.
findings.quote: I worry about junior roles. Writing first drafts is how I learned the job.

themes.name: time savings
themes.description: The participant repeatedly emphasizes how AI reduces routine work and speeds up output.

themes.name: trust and verification
themes.description: They rely on ChatGPT for drafts and summaries but keep checking its accuracy before client use.

themes.name: learning and roles
themes.description: They connect AI not only to efficiency but also to how people, especially juniors, develop skills on the job.

key_points: ChatGPT is part of the participant's daily morning workflow.
A colleague's demonstration was the key trigger for adoption.
The participant reports faster report delivery but remains cautious about errors.
Reliability is the main desired improvement for client work.
They are worried about how AI could affect junior-level learning opportunities.

sentiment.label: mixed
sentiment.rationale: The participant describes clear productivity benefits and time savings, but also strong concerns about hallucinations and impacts on junior roles.
